presets.name: Modern
presets.description: A bunch of enhancements and gameplay tweaks to make the game feel more 'modern'. Not recommended for the first-time players, but it's a great way to re-experience the game.

presets.name: Recommended
presets.description: Settings that keep the core gameplay intact, while adding a bunch of quality of life improvements. Recommended for most players.

presets.name: Vanilla
presets.description: Settings that match perfectly to the original game on the original hardware.

inputPresets.name: Default
inputPresets.description: Default input mapping for XInput controllers and keyboard. Should work well with most controllers!

inputPresets.name: 8BitDo 64 (D)
inputPresets.description: Input mapping for the 8BitDo 64 controller for Analogue 3D. Note that, for some reason, the controller maps the C-buttons to the right stick in D mode.

inputPresets.name: 8BitDo 64 (S)
inputPresets.description: Input mapping for the 8BitDo 64 controller for Analogue's latest 'no emulation' emulation box that managed to sell out instantly. Note that, for some reason, the controller swaps the A and B buttons in S mode, which might cause the launcher to display the wrong button prompts.

inputPresets.name: GameCube Controller (GBros.)
inputPresets.description: Input mapping for the original GameCube controller, using 8BitDo's GBros. adapter.

inputPresets.name: Switch Online N64 Controller
inputPresets.description: Input mapping for the Nintendo's Switch Online N64 Controller.

inputPresets.name: Switch Pro Controller
inputPresets.description: Input mapping for the Nintendo Switch Pro Controller. Not tested with the Switch 2 Pro Controller!

items.description: Makes the game run in fullscreen. Can be toggled in-game via the "Alt + Enter" key combo.
items.name: Fullscreen

items.description: Sets the monitor the game appears on in fullscreen mode.
items.name: Default Monitor

items.description: Toggles VSync to prevent screen tearing. Disabling this might result in a smoother perceived frame rate, but at the cost of screen tearing.
items.name: VSync

items.description: Sets the default width of the game window in pixels.
items.name: Default Window Width

items.description: Sets the default height of the game window in pixels.
items.name: Default Window Height

items.description: Sets the display mode for the fullscreen mode.
items.name: Fullscreen Display Mode

items.description: Sets the base volume for the game's audio output.
items.name: Overall Volume

items.description: Sets the volume of the in-game background music.
items.name: Music Volume

items.description: Sets the volume of various in-game jingles.
items.name: Jingle Volume

items.description: Sets the volume of the sound effects.
items.name: Sound Volume

items.description: Sets the multiplier for the internal resolution. 1x is 240p, 2x is 480p, and so on. Set it to "Display Resolution" to use the same resolution as your display.
items.name: Internal Resolution

items.description: Sets the game's aspect ratio. Set it to "Auto" to use the aspect ratio of your display.
items.name: Aspect Ratio

items.description: Sets the frame rate the game renders at. Animation interpolation is used for higher frame rates, and the game logic always runs at 30 FPS.
items.name: Frame Rate

items.description: Enables multisample anti-aliasing to reduce jagged edges. Higher values provide better quality.
items.name: Anti-Aliasing

items.description: Changes the draw distance for certain objects. Changes to this setting may affect the gameplay in subtle ways, and lead to minor graphical issues.
items.name: Draw Distance

items.description: Sets the level of detail for certain in-game models.
items.name: Level of Detail

items.description: Changes the way the textures are filtered. "3 Point" filtering is what the original hardware uses.
items.name: Texture Filtering

items.description: Enables anisotropic filtering to improve texture quality at oblique angles.
items.name: Anisotropic Filtering

items.description: Changes the type of noise used for transparency effects at higher internal resolutions. "Chunky" gives the most accurate results.
items.name: Noise Type

items.description: Adds a horizontal blur to the image, similar to the original Nintendo 64 hardware (though not completely accurate).
items.name: N64 Blur

items.description: Applies various tweaks to the controls, making them feel tighter and more precise overall.
items.name: Improved Controls

items.description: Applies minor tweaks to the swimming controls, also making them more precise.
items.name: Improved Swimming

items.description: Improves hanging on ceilings by making the movement faster and removing the requirement of holding A.
items.name: Improved Hanging

items.description: Allows you to bounce off the enemies higher by holding A, just like in most other Mario games.
items.name: Enemy Bouncing

items.description: Allows you to control Mario and navigate the menus with the D-Pad.
items.name: D-Pad Controls

items.description: Gives you near full control over Mario's direction in air. This setting significantly alters the way the controls feel and is not recommended for first-time players.
items.name: Full Air Control

items.description: Fixes various gameplay issues present in the original game. Fixing collision issues and exploits will make certain speedrunning tricks impossible.
items.name: Fix Gameplay Bugs

items.description: Saves the number of lives you have to the currently selected save file. In the original game, the number of lives resets each time you load a save file.
items.name: Save Lives to Save File

items.description: Makes Koopa shells and blue coin switches respawn after use.
items.name: Make Items Respawn

items.description: Disables warps that send you back to outside Peach's Castle. This setting also prevents you from getting game overs from those warps to prevent them from becoming unfair.
items.name: Remove Inconvenient Warps

items.description: Makes underwater shells last longer, makes Metal Mario sink faster, and makes Metal Mario's interactions with various objects more consistent.
items.name: Improved Powerups

items.description: Fixes some inconsistencies in the behaviors of some enemies. Specifically Boos, Clams, and Tiny Goombas.
items.name: Improved Enemies

items.description: Makes talking to the NPCs easier and more consistent.
items.name: Improved NPCs

items.description: Prevents you from taking damage after hitting the breakable wall required for the "Blast Away the Wall" mission. Recommended when playing with the "Permadeath Mode" enabled.
items.name: Improved "Blast Away the Wall"

items.description: Makes MIPS return to the castle after you collect 120 Power Stars, with a special message.
items.name: Bring MIPS Back

items.description: Prevents you from taking damage after falling from a distance.
items.name: Disable Fall Damage

items.description: Allows you to leave a course from the pause menu without having to stand still. Do not use this to cheat, that wouldn't be very nice!
items.name: Allow Leaving the Course at Any Time

items.description: Makes Bowser's submarine always appear in the first mission of Dire Dire Docks, and never in the later ones. It's recommended to leave this enabled if you have no idea what any of this is about.
items.name: Tie Bowser's Sub to Missions

items.description: Allows you to continue playing the game after a getting a Power Star, and makes gameplay changes to make it all work.
items.name: Always Stay in Course

items.description: Skips the mission select screen and always chooses the next available mission. Completing all 6 main missions in a course enables the mission select screen again.
items.name: Skip Mission Select

items.description: Makes completing a mission automatically start the next available one.
items.name: Auto Switch to the Next Mission

items.description: Skips some cutscenes that could become repetitive during repeat playthroughs. Not recommended for the first-time players.
items.name: Skip Cutscenes

items.description:
Changes the default camera mode.
The default mode in the original game is "Lakitu Cam".
items.name: Default Camera Mode

items.description:
Changes the alternate camera mode that you can switch to in-game.
The default mode in the original game is "Mario Cam".
items.name: Alternate Camera Mode

items.description: Allows horizontal analog camera movement using the right analog stick and removes most camera movement limits.
items.name: Horizontal Analog Camera

items.description: Allows you to tilt the camera vertically using the right analog stick in the "Custom" camera mode.
items.name: Vertical Analog Camera

items.description: Allows you to rotate the camera with more precision with the C-Buttons.
items.name: Improved C-Button Camera

items.description: Allows you to center the camera behind Mario by pressing L, similarly to the DS version. Doesn't work when the camera is locked.
items.name: Center Camera Button

items.description: Inverts horizontal camera controls when either the "Horizontal Analog Camera" or "Improved C-Button Camera" setting is enabled.
items.name: Invert Horizontal Camera Controls

items.description: Inverts vertical camera controls when the "Vertical Analog Camera" setting is enabled.
items.name: Invert Vertical Camera Controls

items.description:
Sets the movement speed of the analog camera. Also applies to the improved C-Button camera.
The default value is 32.
items.name: Analog Camera Speed

items.description:
Pans the camera further away, regardless of the camera mode.
The default value is 0.
items.name: Additional Camera Distance

items.description:
Adds additional field of view over the original.
The default value is 0.
items.name: Additional FoV

items.description: Fixes various typos in the game's text, including Yoshi's infamous "Mario!!! It that really you???".
items.name: Fix Text Typos

items.description: Adds an "Exit to Desktop" option to the pause menu. It's the little things that make a difference...
items.name: Add Quit Option

items.description: Redesigns the HUD to make better use of the widescreen resolution.
items.name: HUD Layout

items.description: Centers the HUD as if the screen ratio is 4:3. Makes no practical difference when the "Aspect Ratio" is set to "Force 4:3".
items.name: 4:3 HUD

items.description: Shows the stars you've collected in a course in the HUD. Goes well with the "Always Stay in Course" setting.
items.name: Show the Collected Stars

items.description: Adds leading zeroes to things like coin and star counters in the HUD.
items.name: Add Zeroes to Counters

items.description: Always shows the indicator for the 100 coin star in both the mission select screen, and the HUD while the "Show the Collected Stars" setting is enabled.
items.name: Always Show the 100 Coin Star

items.description: Prevents the health bar from hiding automatically. Makes no difference when the "Modern" HUD layout is used.
items.name: Always Show the Health Meter

items.description: Applies texture filtering to the HUD elements. Not recommended with default textures.
items.name: HUD Filtering

items.description: Hides the HUD completely.
items.name: Hide HUD

items.description: Introduces wall sliding from later Mario titles and changes how wall jumping works accordingly.
items.name: Wall Sliding

items.description: Allows you to perform a high jump right after a ground pound, like in recent 3D Mario titles.
items.name: Ground Pound Jump

items.description: Allows you to do short hops and continue sliding after diving by pressing B, just like in Super Mario Sunshine.
items.name: Sunshine Dive Hop

items.description: Allows you to perform the dive move the same way as in Super Mario Odyssey.
items.name: Odyssey Ground Pound Dive

items.description: Keep on rollin' baby, you know what time it is.
items.name: Odyssey Rolling

items.description: Gives Mario a small bounce after landing from a ground pound. You can cancel the bounce by holding Z, or perform a slide by holding a direction. Borrowed from Super Mario Flashback.
items.name: Flashback Ground Pound

items.description: Restores the unused pyramid explosion cutscene in Shifting Sand Land.
items.name: Enable the Unused Pyramid Cutscene

items.description: Restores the Bowser defeat cutscene sound effects, and the unused the trapdoor sound effect for the first star door.
items.name: Restore Unused Sound Effects

items.description: Restores the unused sad-looking eye texture for the mother penguin, as seen in the Shoshinkai 1995 beta footage.
items.name: Restore Mother Penguin's Sad Eyes

items.description: Replaces the regular triple jump with the twirl move, as seen in early gameplay footage.
items.name: Replace Triple Jump w/ Twirl

items.description: Makes the camera behave more like how it did in early gameplay footage, and restores some unused functionality. Might not be 100% accurate.
items.name: Use Beta-like Camera

items.description: Makes Mario sparkle when starting a course, like seen in early gameplay footage.
items.name: Make Mario Sparkle at Course Start

items.description: Restores a bug from the Japanese version of the game where it shows a star when you grab a key after defeating Bowser.
items.name: Replace Keys w/ Stars When Collected

items.description: Makes Mario not lose any health when underwater, and reduces all damage taken by half.
items.name: Casual Mode

items.description: Disables the lives system and makes it impossible to get a Game Over.
items.name: Infinite Lives Mode

items.description: Gives every stage an alternate look via different color palettes, and mirrors them all horizontally. A fun way to replay the original game!
items.name: Encore Mode

items.description: Makes Mario completely invisible, making it hard to exactly tell where he is.
items.name: Invisible Mode

items.description: Makes it so that the only way to heal Mario is to collect a Power Star. Also removes all Spinning Hearts.
items.name: No Healing Mode

items.description: Makes it so that 1-Up Mushrooms kill you instantly. Based on the popular challenge with same name.
items.name: Green Demon Mode

items.description:
Not only removes Mario's cap so he takes more damage, but also makes the bosses and races harder. Perfect for those who are looking for a bit more challenge!
WARNING: If you start a game, or save to an existing save slot with Hard Mode on that save slot will forever be locked at Hard Mode!
items.name: Hard Mode

items.description:
You have only 1 hit point! All you need to die is to get hit once, so be careful! At least you can swim as much as you want...
WARNING: If you start a game, or save to an existing save slot with Daredevil Mode on that save slot will forever be locked at Daredevil Mode!
items.name: Daredevil Mode

items.description:
You have only 1 life! Once you die, your save data gets deleted, with no way to restore it. Only for those who want the ultimate challenge!
WARNING: If you start a game, or save to an existing save slot with Permadeath Mode on that save slot will forever be locked at Permadeath Mode!
items.name: Permadeath Mode

items.description:

items.description:
Enables and sets the strength of the controller rumble effect.
Rumble itself works the same way as the Super Mario 3D All-Stars and the Shindou Edition.

items.description: Disables the support for non-XInput controllers, since they can cause conflicts with certain remapping software (like BetterJoy).

items.description: Allows you to navigate the menus with your mouse. Also works with the camera if you enable the "Analog Camera" settings, and works best with the "Custom" camera mode.

Sets the mouse sensitivity when the "Mouse Support" setting is on.
The default value is 4.

items.description: Makes the launcher start in fullscreen. Does not affect the game itself. Can be toggled via the "Alt + Enter" key combo.
